subject: Proposal: hub-and-satellite org model for core-serving teams
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-15 09:12 -0700
Subject: Proposal: hub-and-satellite org model for core-serving teams

Team —

I ran the pilot hypothesis with the runtime and product leads over the last month and we have a sketch of a hub-and-satellite model that I think addresses three recurring problems: fragmented ownership of shared infra, long cross-team review cycles, and inconsistent oncall / escalation pathways for inference regressions.

Attached are: an org chart that shows a central "Serving Hub" (operations, release, infra stewardship) and 3 "satellite" squad groups aligned to product domains (chat, search, embeddings); a role-scope matrix that proposes what stays in the hub vs what the satellite owns; and a short comms digest for managers.

High-level:
- Hub: service-level SLO ownership, centralized rollout pipelines, kernel/quantization expertise, cost optimization playbook.
- Satellites: product-feature delivery, latency budgets for their domain, owning prompt/eval bundles and quality regressions.
- Reporting: hub engineering manager reports to infra platform lead; satellite tech leads keep dotted lines to the hub for shared primitives.

Asks:
1) Feedback on the role-scope split in the matrix (attached) — I'm particularly unsure about where to draw the line for oncall responsibilities for KV cache corruption incidents.
2) Approve a communications timing: propose an all-hands for affected pods + one-on-one manager briefings next week.

I want this to be a pilot for 3 months with explicit success metrics (deployment time, mean time to rollback, cross-domain release coordination time). If acceptable, I'll turn this into a short Confluence playbook and start chef-ing the pilot tickets.

Thanks —
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Director, Serving Architecture
Redwood Inference

Attachments: hub-satellite-org-chart.pdf, role-scope-matrix.xlsx, comm-plan-digest.txt

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-15 11:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: hub-and-satellite org model for core-serving teams

Sofia —

Appreciate the clear framing and the attachments. Quick thoughts:

- The hub/satellite split looks sensible for infra stewardship, but we should be explicit about promotion/career ladder impacts for engineers who move into hub roles. Historically those moves have felt like lateral "platform" sinks.
- Can we add a section on escalation timelines? The matrix currently says "hub owns rollback" but does not define time-to-ack or time-to-fix responsibilities.
- For comms, we need a templated FAQ for people managers (questions around performance review implications, who signs off on OKRs, and temporary reassignments).

I'll flag potential pushback from some product leads if their satellites lose direct release control; we should be ready with a rollback policy that keeps product velocity during the pilot.

+1 on the 3-month pilot with measurable SLAs.

—Grace
Grace O'Connor
VP, Product
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-16 08:27 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: hub-and-satellite org model for core-serving teams

All —

A couple of operational notes from product infra perspective:
1) We should schedule a joint review with Security & Compliance before any hub takes on centralized rollback capabilities — will loop in legal if we surface data retention changes.
2) For the satellites, define "fast rollback knobs" that product teams can trigger without hub intervention for customer-facing regressions. That preserves product-owner agency.
3) Curious if anyone has a prior example of banding a core infra team as "hub" without impacting IC promotion. Grace's point is real — we need clear promotion criteria (e.g., ownership impact, cross-team mentorship).

I'll draft a short addendum on quick rollback paths and share by tomorrow.

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Product Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-17 10:41 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: hub-and-satellite org model for core-serving teams

Sofia —

Thanks for running this. Operationally, a couple of nitty items from HR coordination side:
- Performance reviews: we need a delegated manager plan — who will write reviews for hub engineers who have dotted-line ownership to product? Recommend primary manager in the hub write the review with satellite leads providing input; put that process in writing.
- Role scope: the role-scope matrix should include examples of impact statements to use in promo packets for either individual contributor or engineering manager tracks.
- Sensitive transitions: for any people moving teams, HR would like 2-week private manager-to-manager transitions and an agreed handover note to prevent surprises.

I can draft the delegated-review template and a handover checklist if the draft moves forward.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of People Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-19 14:02 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: hub-and-satellite org model for core-serving teams

Folks —

I've pulled a quick risk register and a suggested rollout timeline into the shared Drive (link in thread). Top three risks:
1) Morale dip on reassignments if not paired with transparent compensation/promo language.
2) Operational confusion during first two sprints when incident runbooks are not fully aligned.
3) Customer-facing SLAs may need temporary carve-outs for satellites while they adopt hub tooling.

Proposed mitigations: clear manager comms, a 30/60/90-day checklist for satellites, and a small "response" rotation inside the hub for the pilot period to triage cross-satellite incidents.

If we agree on the mitigations, I'd like to lock the pilot start for Aug 2 and run two-week syncs to report metrics.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: role-scope-matrix.xlsx

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-20 16:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: hub-and-satellite org model for core-serving teams

Thanks, everyone — great feedback.

Decisions from thread:
- Pilot locked: Aug 2 start; 3-month duration with 2-week sync cadence.
- HR will publish delegated-review template and handover checklist (Marissa to lead).
- Jonas to publish quick-rollback addendum and Security signoff checklist.
- Hub will staff a single-response rotation for the pilot window; Karthik to propose rotation schedule.

Next steps: I'll move the doc set to Confluence and publish the comms draft for managers by Monday EOD. If there are no objections, I'll send the manager-facing announcement on Tue morning and schedule the all-hands.

Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Director, Serving Architecture
Redwood Inference
